entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1. The revision petitioner/accused was convicted by the Court below for the offence under Section 16(1A) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short 'the Act') vide judgment in C.C.No.71 of 2007 dated 23.06.2008 by the learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Nalgonda.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Nalgonda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In appeal, the learned Sessions Judge confirmed the said conviction vide judgment in Criminal Appeal No.109 of 2008 dated 30.12.2009.
2.
The case of the Food Inspector is that on 11.07.2006, he went to the shop of the petitioner M/s.Srinivasa Traders, of which the petitioner was the Proprietor.
He purchased six sealed polythene packets containing Mustard seeds.
The said seeds were kept for sale for human consumption.
3. The Inspector purchased six packets and made them into three packets by opening the sealed packets and sent them for analysis to FSL.

4. The only ground raised by the learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioner is that under Rule 22 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, if the food is sold in packaged condition or in sealed container or package, they should be sent for analysis in its original condition without opening the package.

As seen from the Note to Rule 22-A of the Rules reads as follows:
"Note: Foods sold in packaged condition (Sealed container/package) shall be sent for analysis in its condition without opening the package and along with original label to constitute the approximate quantity."
5.
Since it is apparent from the evidence of P.W.1/Food Inspector that the sealed packets were cut open for sampling and sent for analysis, which is in violation of Rule 22 of the Rules.
For the said reason, the revision deserves to be allowed.
6. In the result, judgment of trial Court in Criminal Appeal No.109 of 2008 dated 30.12.2009 is hereby set aside.
Since the appellant is on bail, his bail bonds shall stand cancelled.
